Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:11:1.hebrew: ישיב - כסף ישיב לבעליו, דהוה ליה למיכתב: בעל הבור ישלם כסף לבעליו. ישיב דכתב רחמנא למה לי, הואיל וכבר כתיב ישלם? לרבות כל השבות:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:11:1.english: He shall restore - [The verse states:] "Money he shall restore to its owner," for it should have written: "The owner of the pit shall pay money to its owner." Why do I need "he shall restore" that the Merciful One wrote, since "he shall pay" is already written? [It comes] to include all items of equivalent value.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:12:1.hebrew: מדעתו - אי משלם ליה מזיק נזקו מדעתו, דלא אטרחיה לצעוק עליו בב"ד, שקיל סובין. אבל אם אינו רוצה המזיק לשלם נזקו לניזק אלא בב"ד, דהיינו בעל כרחו, אינו משלם אלא כסף:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:12:1.english: Of his own volition - If the damager pays him his damages of his own volition, so that he did not trouble him to cry out against him in court, [the injured party] takes bran. But if the damager does not want to pay his damages to the injured party except in court, that is, against his will, he pays only money.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:13:1.hebrew: דיקא נמי - דגבי מיטב כתיב ישלם, דמשמע ישלם בעל כרחו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:13:1.english: [The wording] is also precise - For regarding "the best" [land], it is written "he shall pay," which implies he shall pay against his will.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:14:1.hebrew: ישולם - משמע על ידי אחרים, דב"ד יורדין לנכסיו דמזיק, אבל ישלם משמע נמי מדעתו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:14:1.english: It shall be paid - [This] implies [that it is paid] by others, for the court descends to the property of the damager, but "he shall pay" also implies [that he pays] of his own volition.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:15:1.hebrew: אלא אמר אביי - לא משכחת תירוצא להני קראי אלא כדמר, כי האי גוונא דתרצה רבה להך דתניא כו':
Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:15:1.english: Rather, Abaye said - You cannot find a resolution to these verses except in accordance with the Master, in the manner that Rabba resolved that [baraita] which is taught, etc.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:15:2.hebrew: מי שהיו לו שדות בתים וכרמים - שוה מאתים זוז. ותנן במסכת פאה (פ"ח מ"ח): מי שיש לו מאתים זוז לא יטול לקט, שכחה, ופאה, ומעשר עני, דלאו עני הוא, ונמצא גוזל עניים. היו לו מאתים זוז חסר דינר, ונתנו לו שוה אלף זוז בבת אחת, הרי זה יטול. וזה יש לו בתים, שדות, וכרמים שוה מאתים זוז, אבל אינו מוצא למכור, מאכילין אותו מעשר עני עד מחצה, שוה מאה זוז, וקרקעותיו ימכור במאה זוז, דטפי מפלגא לא זיילי לעולם, והרי יש לו מאתים זוז:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:15:2.english: One who had fields, houses, and vineyards - [Worth] two hundred zuz. And we learned in a mishna in Tractate Pe'ah (8:8): One who has two hundred zuz may not take gleanings, forgotten sheaves, pe'ah, or poor man's tithe, for he is not poor, and he would turn out to be robbing the poor. [If] he had two hundred zuz minus one dinar, and they gave him [an amount] worth one thousand zuz all at once, he may take [it]. And this [person] has houses, fields, and vineyards worth two hundred zuz, but he cannot find [a buyer] to sell [them to]; we feed him poor man's tithe up to half, [i.e.,] worth one hundred zuz, and his lands he will sell for one hundred zuz, for [lands] never depreciate by more than half, and behold, he has two hundred zuz.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:16:1.english: And the Master discussed it - And that is Rabba.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:16:2.hebrew: אפילו טובא נמי ליספו ליה - שהרי עכשיו אין שוה מאתים זוז, ותנן (שם): היו לו מאתים זוז חסר דינר, אפילו נתנו לו שוה אלף זוז בבת אחת, יטול:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:16:2.english: Let them feed him even more as well - For now [his property] is not worth two hundred zuz, and we learned [in the mishna] there: [If] he had two hundred zuz minus one dinar, even if they gave him the value of a thousand zuz at one time, he may take [it].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:1:1.english: And a creditor, his law is [to collect] from intermediate-quality [land] - [This is taught] in Tractate Gittin, in chapter HaNizakin (Gittin 48b).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:2:1.hebrew: וכי תימא קסבר ר"ע כו' - אפילו הכי לא גמרינן הקדש מיניה, דאיכא למיפרך: מה לב"ח שכן יפה כחו בנזקין, שההדיוט הוא נוטל בהזיקו מן העידית:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:2:1.english: And if you would say that Rabbi Akiva holds, etc. - Even so, we do not derive [the law of] consecrated property from it, for it can be refuted: What [is true] of a creditor? That his power is enhanced with regard to damages, for an ordinary person collects from superior-quality land for damage done to him.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:2:2.english: Can you say [the same] of consecrated property, whose power is weakened with regard to damages - For it does not collect any damages at all.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:4:1.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya, etc. - [This is taught] at the beginning of our chapter of "An Ox That Gored [Four and Five]."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:4:2.hebrew: משלם נזק שלם - וקדריש ליה לרעהו הכי: שור של רעהו הוא דכי הוי מזיק תם לא משלם אלא חצי נזק, אבל אי מזיק שור של הקדש, משלם מזיק נזק שלם, ואפילו תם. וקאמר ר"ע דשקל הקדש שיעור דמי שורו מעידית קרקעות של מזיק:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:4:2.english: Pays full damage - And [Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya] expounds [the word] "his neighbor" as follows: It is [specifically] an ox belonging to his neighbor [where], when the damaging ox is innocuous, [its owner] pays only half damage; but if it damages an ox belonging to consecrated property, the damager pays full damage, even [if it was] innocuous. And Rabbi Akiva says that consecrated property collects the amount of the value of its ox from the superior-quality land of the damager.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:5:1.hebrew: דלמא דכ"ע בדניזק שיימינן - ולא משלם ליה מזיק אלא זיבורית, הואיל והוא כעידית דניזק, דמודה ר"ע לר' ישמעאל, דאמר מיטב שדהו של ניזק, ועידית דקאמר ר"ע, עידית דניזק קאמר, ולא אתי לאיפלוגי עליה אלא בהקדש:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:5:1.english: Perhaps everyone agrees that we appraise based on [the land of] the injured party - And the damager pays him only inferior-quality land, since it is equivalent to the superior-quality land of the injured party, for Rabbi Akiva agrees with Rabbi Yishmael, who said [that the verse] "the best of his field" [refers to that] of the injured party; and [when] Rabbi Akiva said "superior-quality land," he meant the superior-quality land of the injured party, and he did not come to disagree with him except regarding consecrated property.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:5:2.hebrew: ובפלוגתא דר"ש בן מנסיא ורבנן פליגי - דשמעיה ר"ע לרבי ישמעאל דלא איירי אלא בהדיוט, אבל בנזקי הקדש פטר ליה, ואתי ר"ע לפלוגי עליה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:5:2.english: And they disagree with regard to the dispute between Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya and the Rabbis - For Rabbi Akiva heard that Rabbi Yishmael was speaking only of [damage caused to] an ordinary person, but regarding damage to consecrated property he exempted [the damager], and Rabbi Akiva came to disagree with him.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:7:1.hebrew: א"כ מאי לא בא הכתוב - דמשמע דבקרא גופיה פליגי, דלא בא הכתוב להכי, אלמא בהדיוט נמי פליגי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:7:1.english: If so, what is [the meaning of] "The verse did not come" - For it implies that they disagree about the verse itself, [saying] that the verse did not come for this [purpose]; consequently, they disagree regarding an ordinary person as well.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:8:1.hebrew: ועוד מאי ק"ו להקדש - הואיל ומן העידית דקאמר ר' עקיבא אניזק קאי, ולאקולי אתא דיהיב ליה מזיק מזיבורית, מאי ק"ו להקדש? גריעותא הוי! ולר"ע יפה כחו דהקדש בנזקין, דאמר דאפילו הוי מזיק תם שקיל הקדש נזק שלם, ונפקא ליה מרעהו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:8:1.english: And furthermore, what is [the meaning of] "an a fortiori [inference] for consecrated property"? - Since "from the best [land]" that Rabbi Akiva stated refers to the injured party, and it comes to be lenient [toward the damager], [such] that the damager gives him of [his] inferior-quality [land], what is [the meaning of] "an a fortiori [inference] for consecrated property"? It is a disadvantage [for consecrated property]! And according to Rabbi Akiva, the power of consecrated property is enhanced with regard to damages, as he says that even if the damaging [ox] was innocuous, consecrated property collects full damages, and he derives this from "his fellow".

Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:9:1.hebrew: ועוד - תניא בהדיא, דמן העידית דקאמר ר"ע אמזיק קאי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 7a:9:1.english: And furthermore - It is taught explicitly that "from the best" which Rabbi Akiva stated refers to the damager.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 7a:11:1.hebrew: ישיב לרבות שוה כסף - בפ"ק דקדושין (דף ח. טז.) דרשינן נמי הכי גבי עבד עברי, ויש [שום] צריכותא (ע"ש דף ב. בתוספות ד"ה בפרוטה):
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 7a:11:1.english: "He shall restore" to include that which is equivalent to money - In the first chapter of Kiddushin (8a, 16a), we also derive this regarding a Hebrew slave (eved ivri), and there is [some] necessity [for both] (see there, 2a, in Tosafot, s.v. "Biprutah").

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 7a:14:1.hebrew: ישלם מדעתו משמע - וא"ת: דבפרק הזרוע (חולין ד' קל: ושם ד"ה תנא) ישלם בעל כרחו משמע, דקאמר: תנא תני ישלם דברי ר' אליעזר, ואת אמרת מדת חסידות שנו כאן? וי"ל: דהתם לא קאמר אלא דלא הוי מדת חסידות, אלא בדין חייב. ועוד אמר ר"ת, דה"ק: תנא תני ישלם דברי רבי אליעזר, ופליגי רבנן עליה, ואת אמרת וכו', ועל מדת חסידות לא הוו פליגי רבנן. ובלאו הכי צריך לפרש התם כן:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 7a:14:1.english: "He shall pay" implies of his own volition - And if you say: In Perek HaZero'a (Chullin 130b, and there s.v. Tanna), "he shall pay" implies against his will, for it says: "The Tanna teaches: 'He shall pay' — the words of Rabbi Eliezer, and you say [that] they taught a measure of piety here"? And one can say that there, it means only that it is not a measure of piety, but rather by law he is obligated. And furthermore, Rabbeinu Tam said that this is what it means: The Tanna teaches: "He shall pay" — the words of Rabbi Eliezer, and the Rabbis dispute him, and you say etc. [that they taught a measure of piety here] — and over a measure of piety the Rabbis would not have disputed! And even without this, it is necessary to explain there in this manner.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 7a:15:1.hebrew: מי שהיו לו בתים כו' - לא מיירי בבתים שדר בהם, דהא תנן במסכת פאה (פ"ח מ"ח): אין מחייבין אותו למכור ביתו וכלי תשמישו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 7a:15:1.english: One who had houses, etc. - [This] is not dealing with houses that he lives in, for we learned in a Mishnah in Tractate Peah (8:8): "We do not obligate him to sell his house and his utensils of use."

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 7a:16:1.hebrew: אי דאייקור ארעתא אפילו פורתא נמי לא ליספו ליה - אף על גב שאינו מוצא ליתן עליהם מאתים זוז, לא יטול כלל, לפי שגרם לעצמו ופשע, דלא הוי ליה למיעל ולמיפק אזוזי; אבל אם לא פשע, אפילו שוות יותר ממאתים זוז, יכול ליטול קודם שימכור בפחות משויין. ורב אלפס מפרש בעשיר, ועד מחצה היינו: עד שימצא שיקנה אותם לכל הפחות בחצי דמיהן. וגרסינן בתר הכי: אילימא דזיל ארעתא דכ"ע ודידיה נמי זל בהדייהו, אפילו פורתא נמי לא ליספו ליה? פירוש: אפילו הוזלו כל כך שאפילו המחצה לא יתנו לו, לא ליספו ליה, כיון דזל ארעתא דכ"ע, ושוות מאתים זוז אף לפי הזול. אלא דאייקור כ"ע, אפילו טובא נמי ליספו ליה? פי': אפילו מוצא שיתנו טפי ממחצה, מ"מ ליספו ליה עד שימצא למוכרן בשויין, דמה שאין מוצא למוכרן בשויין — לפי שרואין אותו שהוא דחוק. ואית דגרס: אי דזולי כו' אפילו טובא נמי לא ליספו ליה? פי': אפילו הוזלו הרבה, לא ליספו ליה, כיון דשוות מאתים זוז, וזול נמי דכ"ע; ואי דאייקור, אפילו פורתא ליספו ליה? פירוש: אפילו הוזלו פורתא:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 7a:16:1.english: If the land appreciated, even a little bit they should not feed him either - Even though he cannot find [anyone willing] to give two hundred zuz for them, he may not take [poor man's tithe] at all, because he brought it upon himself and was negligent, for he should not have gone in and out for money. But if he was not negligent, even if [his properties] are worth more than two hundred zuz, he may take [tithe] before selling [them] for less than their value. And Rav Alfas [the Rif] explains [the Baraita as referring] to a wealthy person, and "until half" means until he finds [someone] who will buy them for at least half their value. And we have the reading after this: "If we say that everyone's land depreciated, and his also depreciated along with theirs, they should not feed him even a small amount?" Explanation: Even if they depreciated so much that they will not give him even half [their value], they should not feed him [tithe], since everyone's land depreciated and [his property] is worth two hundred zuz even according to the depreciated price. "Rather, that everyone's [land] appreciated — they should feed him even a lot?" Explanation: Even if he finds [buyers] who would give more than half, nevertheless they should feed him [tithe] until he finds [someone] to sell them to at their full value, for the fact that he cannot find [someone] to sell them to at their full value is because they see that he is hard-pressed [for money]. And there are those who read: "If they depreciated, etc., they should not feed him even a lot?" Explanation: Even if they depreciated greatly, they should not feed him, since [his property] is worth two hundred zuz and everyone's [land] also depreciated; "And if [everyone else's land] appreciated, they should feed him even a little bit?" Explanation: Even if they depreciated [only] a little bit.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 7a:3:1.hebrew: ורבי עקיבא סבר לה כר' שמעון - תימה: לעיל (בבא קמא דף ה.), כי מוקי לה עדים זוממין כר"ע, ליקשי: אי ר"ע, ליתני תרי גווני שור: שור דאזיק שור דהדיוט, ושור דאזיק שור דהקדש? וי"ל: דבהקדש לא קמיירי. אך קשה: כי נמי סבר כר"ש, לפרוך: מה להדיוט שכן יפה כחו בנזקי אדם? ולמאי דפי', דלא דרשינן כי יאכל פרט למזיק דלא משלם כלל, אלא משום דכתיב רעהו — אתי שפיר. אך קשה, ולפרוך: שכן יפה כחו בנזקי בור:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 7a:3:1.english: And Rabbi Akiva holds in accordance with Rabbi Shimon - It is puzzling: Above (Bava Kamma 5a), when [the Gemara] establishes [the omission of] conspiring witnesses in accordance with Rabbi Akiva, let [the Gemara] ask: If [Rabbi Oshaya holds like] Rabbi Akiva, let him teach two types of ox: an ox that damaged the ox of a common person (hedyot), and an ox that damaged the ox of consecrated property (hekdesh)? And one can say that [Rabbi Oshaya] does not deal with consecrated property. However, it is difficult: Even if [Rabbi Akiva] holds in accordance with Rabbi Shimon [ben Menasya], let [the Gemara] refute [the a fortiori argument]: What [is notable] about a common person? That his power is enhanced with regard to damages [caused by] man! And according to what was explained — that we do not expound "when [a man] eats" (ki yochal) [as] excluding a damager [such] that he does not pay at all, but rather [the exemption is] because it is written "his fellow" (re'ehu) — it works out well. However, it is difficult: But let [the Gemara] refute [it instead: What is notable about a common person?] That his power is enhanced with regard to damages of a pit (bor)!

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 7a:8:1.hebrew: ועוד מאי ק"ו להקדש - פירש הקונטרס: הואיל ומן העידית דא"ר עקיבא אניזק קאי, ולאקולא אתא, דיהיב ליה מזיק מזיבורית, מאי ק"ו להקדש? גריעותא הוא. וקשה לפי': דאין זה גריעותא אלא חומרא, דר"י פוטר לגמרי מזיק את ההקדש, ור"ע מחייבו נ"ש; ולענין מיטב נמי חשיבות הוא, דמשלם ממיטב דניזק ולא מגרוע דניזק. ונראה לר"י דה"פ: מאי ק"ו להקדש? דלענין חיובא מזיק בהקדש לא קאמר, דהא מקרא דר"ש נפקא; אלא לענין מיטב קאמר. ולא הוה לר"ע לאהדורי לרבי ישמעאל ק"ו להקדש, כיון דרבי ישמעאל היה מודה בכך, אי לאו משום דפטר ליה לגמרי:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 7a:8:1.english: And furthermore, what is "an a fortiori to consecrated property" - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: Since [the phrase] "from the superior [land]" that Rabbi Akiva stated refers to the injured party, and it comes as a leniency—that the damager gives him from [his own] inferior [land]—what is "an a fortiori to consecrated property"? It is a detriment! And this explanation is difficult, for this is not a detriment but a stringency: for Rabbi Yishmael completely exempts one who damages consecrated property, whereas Rabbi Akiva holds him liable for full damages (nezek shalem); and regarding best-quality land (meitav) as well, it is an advantage, for he pays from the best of the injured party and not from the poorest of the injured party. And it appears to the Ri that this is the explanation: "What is an a fortiori to consecrated property?" For with regard to the liability of one who damages consecrated property, he [Rabbi Akiva] could not be speaking, as that is derived from the verse of Rabbi Shimon [ben Menasya]; rather, with regard to best-quality land (meitav) he is speaking. And Rabbi Akiva should not have replied to Rabbi Yishmael with an a fortiori to consecrated property, since Rabbi Yishmael would agree to this, were it not that he exempts him completely.
